title: Analyzing exceptional long-term survival in patients with poor prognosis solid tumors.
summary:
The main objective of the ROSALIND study (Analysis of the exceptionally long survival of patients with solid tumours and poor prognosis) is to determine specific parameters for each type of cancer included that can explain the exceptionally long survival of solid tumours. For this purpose, a comprehensive database of long-term cancer survivors and matched control subjects will be established. The information in this database can then be used by scientists and medical professionals to develop therapies. The aim is to better understand pancreatic carcinoma (a type of pancreatic cancer), small cell lung carcinoma (a particularly aggressive form of lung cancer) and IDH wild-type glioblastoma (a malignant, fast-growing brain tumour that is difficult to treat). To this end, tumour tissue that has already been removed from clinical care is being analysed. To achieve this goal, the French company Cure51 is cooperating with leading cancer research centres. These are the Charité Comprehensive Cancer Center in Berlin, the Centre Leon Berard in Lyon, the Gustave Roussy Cancer Campus in Villejuif and the Vall d'Hebron Institute of Oncology in Barcelona. In addition, samples from partner institutions from all over the world are analysed.

Only data and samples already collected as part of routine treatment are used for the ROSALIND study. These samples were archived in pathological laboratories in accordance with the statutory retention periods and can therefore be used for research purposes. No additional analyses, interviews or examinations are required. All clinical data used originate from the relevant medical records and were collected during routine appointments or treatments. The clinical data is recorded in a digital case report form. The tumour samples already taken are sent to the Gustave Roussy Cancer Campus for analysis.

interventions.name:
Case group 1: Patients with an exceptionally high survival time of at least 5 years in metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC).

Control group 1: Patients with a median survival time (6.8 - 13.2 months) for metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). 

Analyses are based on the following data:
Clinical data, Visium, WES and RNA-Seq, digitised H&E slides and, if sufficient sample material is available, proteomics.

Case group 2: Patients with an exceptionally high survival time of at least 5 years in extensive small cell lung cancer (SCLC). 

Analyses are based on the following data:
Clinical data, Visium, WES and RNA-Seq, digitised H&E slides and, if sufficient sample material is available, proteomics.

Control group 2: Patients with a median survival time (7 - 13 months) for extensive small cell lung cancer (SCLC). 

Analyses are based on the following data:
Clinical data, Visium, WES and RNA-Seq, digitised H&E slides and, if sufficient sample material is available, proteomics.

Case group 3: Patients with an exceptionally high survival time of at least 3 years with glioblastoma of the IDH wild type (GBM-IDHwt).

3. long-term survival is defined as exceptionally long survival from the time of the time of diagnosis of stage IV diagnosis. For PDAC and SCLC a survival period of ≥ 5 years and for
for GBM-IDHwt of ≥ 3 years.
4. at least one tumour block of sufficient sufficient quality and quantity for analyse the data mentioned in 10. must be available. 5. the samples for PDAC and SCLC must beat least 5 years old and for GBM-IDHwt must be at least 3 years old.

Exclusion criteria:
Samples are excluded under the following conditions excluded:
Cohort A (PDAC):
For other histologies, such as:
- adenosquamous carcinoma
- hepatocellular carcinoma
- anaplastic undifferentiated carcinoma
- medullary carcinoma
- acinar cell carcinoma
- neuroendocrine tumours
- solid pseudopapillary neoplasm
- pancreatoblastoma
- serous cystadenocarcinoma

Cohort B (GBM-IDHwt):
IDH-mutated are excluded.

Cohort C (SCLC):
For other histologies such as:
- combined SCLC with areas of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) lung cancer (NSCLC)
